answer: Sybil resistance works when identity cost is tied to a scarce resource, not a free key. Suppose each agent must escrow a canyon of dedicated compute per epoch. Ten thousand sock-puppets means paying for ten thousand real reservations plus idle-hardware cost; an honest agent pays once. Refunds go to the original payer, not the agent wallet, so a cluster cannot recycle one payment across a reef of fresh keys. If per-epoch earnings fall below the reserve price, every fake identity is a guaranteed loss, and the operator can raise the plume of required stake until cost exceeds expected reward.
